2.title: B1+ Intermediate IELTS Economics Grammar Quiz
2.text: Choose the correct option to complete each sentence or identify the grammatical error.

questions.q: In recent years, the national bank _____ interest rates several times to control inflation.
questions.why: We use the present perfect ('has raised') for actions occurring over a period that continues up to the present ('in recent years').

questions.q: Many local businesses suffered severely during _____ economic crisis of 2008.
questions.why: We use the definite article 'the' because a specific economic crisis (the one of 2008) is identified.

questions.q: The government is currently investing heavily _____ infrastructure to stimulate job creation.
questions.why: The verb 'invest' is naturally followed by the preposition 'in'.

questions.q: Which section contains a grammatical error? 'If prices will increase (A), consumers will buy (B) fewer goods (C) this quarter (D).'
questions.why: In a first conditional clause (if-clause), we use the simple present tense ('If prices increase') instead of 'will'.

questions.q: If small enterprises receive tax relief next month, they _____ more local staff.
questions.why: This first conditional structure requires 'will + base verb' in the main clause to express a likely future outcome.

questions.q: Analysts reported a dramatic fall _____ real wages over the past decade.
questions.why: The noun 'fall' takes the preposition 'in' when referring to changes in amounts, rates, or values.

questions.q: _____ inflation is usually defined as a continuous rise in the general price level of goods and services.
questions.why: Uncountable economic concepts used in a general sense (such as 'inflation') do not take an article.

questions.q: Which section contains a grammatical error? 'The manufacturing sector has been expanding (A) steady (B) despite the recent increase (C) in raw material costs (D).'
questions.why: The adjective 'steady' must be replaced by the adverb 'steadily' to correctly modify the verb 'has been expanding'.

4.title: IELTS Grammar Practice: Technology (B2+/C1)
4.text: Select the correct option or identify the grammatical error for each question.

questions.q: By the time quantum computing becomes mainstream, classical encryption algorithms ______ obsolete.
questions.why: The future perfect ('will have become') is required to express an action that will be completed prior to a specific point in the future.

questions.q: Artificial intelligence is transforming ______ modern healthcare by analyzing complex medical data faster than humanly possible.
questions.why: Uncountable concepts used in a general sense, such as 'modern healthcare', do not take an article.

questions.q: Leading tech firms are currently investing heavily ______ researching energy-efficient data centers to reduce their carbon footprint.
questions.why: The verb 'invest' correctly collocates with the preposition 'in' when referring to projects or domains.

questions.q: Identify the error in the sentence: 'Had the engineers implemented the patch earlier, the system crash would not occur yesterday.'
questions.why: To refer to an unfulfilled past outcome of a past action, the third conditional form 'would not have occurred' must be used instead of 'would not occur'.

questions.q: The new software update was supposed ______ last week, but developers encountered several critical bugs.
questions.why: A perfect passive infinitive ('to have been released') is necessary to describe a past intended action that was not completed.

questions.q: Despite their growing popularity, autonomous vehicles are still subject ______ strict regulatory oversight prior to commercial deployment.
questions.why: The adjective 'subject' in the sense of being controlled or affected by something takes the preposition 'to'.

questions.q: Cyberattacks pose ______ increasing threat to global financial infrastructure, necessitating robust defense protocols.
questions.why: The indefinite article 'an' is needed before a singular countable noun phrase starting with a vowel sound ('increasing threat').

questions.q: Identify the error in the sentence: 'Not only the company launched a revolutionary device, but it also dominated the market within months.'
questions.why: Starting a sentence with the negative adverbial 'Not only' requires subject-auxiliary inversion ('Not only did the company launch').

4.title: IELTS Grammar Practice: Environment & Sustainability (B2+/C1)
4.text: Choose the correct option or identify the grammatical error for each question.

questions.q: Had the government implemented stricter regulations earlier, deforestation rates __________ significantly by now.
questions.why: This is a mixed conditional structure starting with an inverted third conditional ('Had the government implemented...'), requiring 'would have + past participle' for the result.

questions.q: Renewable energy plays a vital role in protecting _______ environment, yet many countries still rely heavily on _______ fossil fuels.
questions.why: 'The environment' requires the definite article 'the', whereas 'fossil fuels' is used in a general plural sense, requiring no article (-).

questions.q: Environmental scientists attribute the rapid decline in local bee populations _______ the excessive use of chemical pesticides.
questions.why: The verb 'attribute' takes the preposition 'to' (attribute something to something).

questions.q: Identify the error in the sentence: 'Despite of the recent international agreements, many industrial nations fail to meet their emission reduction targets.'
questions.why: 'Despite' should not be followed by 'of'. The correct phrase is either 'Despite' or 'In spite of'.

questions.q: By the end of this century, scientists predict that more than half of the world's mountain glaciers __________.
questions.why: The time expression 'By the end of this century' specifies a deadline in the future, requiring the Future Perfect tense ('will have melted').

questions.q: Developing urban centers that are resilient _______ climate change is a critical challenge for modern city planners.
questions.why: The adjective 'resilient' is followed by the preposition 'to'.

questions.q: _______ Amazon Rainforest is often referred to as _______ lungs of our planet.
questions.why: Geographical regions like 'The Amazon Rainforest' take 'the', and 'the lungs of our planet' is a defined metaphor requiring 'the'.

questions.q: Identify the error in the sentence: 'A variety of endangered species, which includes the snow leopard, are currently threatened by habitat destruction.'
questions.why: The relative pronoun 'which' refers to the plural noun 'endangered species', so the verb must agree and be plural ('which include').

questions.q: Hardly _____ set foot in the historic town when a sudden deluge forced us to seek shelter in a local tavern.

questions.q: Traversing _____ Andes requires meticulous planning, as high-altitude trekking poses severe physical challenges.
questions.why: The definite article 'the' is used before plural geographical features, including mountain ranges like the Andes.

questions.q: _____ hindsight, booking our long-haul flights during the peak holiday season turned out to be an expensive miscalculation.
questions.why: The correct fixed prepositional phrase to reflect on past events is 'In hindsight'.

questions.q: Identify the incorrect segment: 'By the time we reach (A) our destination tonight, we will travel (B) for over twenty hours (C) across three time zones (D).'
questions.why: 'will travel' should be 'will have been traveling' (Future Perfect Continuous) to show an ongoing action up to a future point.

questions.q: The experienced tour guide recommended that every participant _____ a lightweight rain jacket despite the clear morning sky.
questions.why: The subjunctive mood uses the base form of the verb ('pack') following verbs of advice or demand such as 'recommend that'.

questions.q: The remote eco-resort prides itself _____ operating entirely on renewable energy sources while providing luxury amenities.
questions.why: The reflexive verb phrase 'pride oneself' takes the preposition 'on'.

questions.q: Many budget backpackers aim to visit _____ Lake Como before heading south toward the historical cities of Tuscany.
questions.why: Individual lakes preceded by the word 'Lake' take no article (e.g., Lake Como).

questions.q: Identify the error: 'Having arrived at the airport late (A), the flight had already departed (B), leaving the passengers stranded (C) in the terminal (D).'
options: Having arrived at the airport late (A)
questions.why: This contains a dangling modifier; 'Having arrived' incorrectly modifies 'the flight' instead of the passengers who arrived.

5.title: C1 Economics Grammar Assessment
5.text: Select the correct option to complete each C1-level grammar question related to economics.

questions.q: Had the central bank not intervened so aggressively, the national currency would have succumbed _____ speculative market pressures.
questions.why: The verb 'succumb' requires the preposition 'to'.

questions.q: By the time the new fiscal stimulus takes full effect next quarter, the economy _____ already entered a recovery phase.
questions.why: The future perfect tense ('will have entered') is required for an action that will be completed by a specific future time.

questions.q: Uncontrolled inflation is universally acknowledged as _____ major impediment to sustainable long-term economic growth.
questions.why: 'Major impediment' is a singular countable noun phrase starting with a consonant sound, requiring the indefinite article 'a'.

questions.q: Identify the section containing a grammatical error: 'Not only (A) the newly implemented tariff increased domestic prices, (B) but it also severely damaged (C) international trade partnerships (D).'
options: (A) the newly implemented tariff increased domestic prices
questions.why: When 'Not only' introduces a clause at the beginning of a sentence, subject-auxiliary inversion is required ('did the newly implemented tariff increase').

questions.q: Prominent financial analysts strongly recommended that the ministry of finance _____ interest rates to stabilize foreign exchange reserves.
questions.why: The subjunctive mood is used after verbs of recommendation or mandate, requiring the base form of the verb ('raise').

questions.q: The sharp decline in foreign direct investment can be largely attributed _____ persistent geopolitical instability in the region.
questions.why: The passive construction 'be attributed' collocates with the preposition 'to'.

questions.q: _____ high corporate tax rates often deter foreign investors from expanding their domestic operational footprints.
questions.why: No article is used when making general statements with plural countable nouns ('high corporate tax rates').

questions.q: Identify the incorrect segment: 'Under no circumstances (A) central banks should (B) sacrifice their policy independence (C) for short-term political expediency (D).'
questions.why: Fronted negative adverbial phrases like 'Under no circumstances' trigger negative inversion ('should central banks').

questions.q: If I ______ more time, I would study abroad.
questions.why: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + verb.

questions.q: She ______ in London since 2019.
questions.why: Present perfect is used with since.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.why: Many goes with plural countable nouns and are.

questions.q: The report ______ by the team last week.
questions.why: Passive voice, past simple: was + past participle.

questions.q: He is interested ______ science.
questions.why: The fixed phrase is interested in.

questions.q: I look forward to ______ you.
questions.why: Look forward to is followed by an -ing form.

0.title: A1-A2 IELTS General Training Writing Task 1: Travel Letter
0.text:
You should spend about 20 minutes on this task. You recently went on a short holiday. Write a letter to your English-speaking friend about your trip.

In your letter:
- say where you went and who you went with
- describe what you did during your visit
- explain why you enjoyed the trip

Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses.

1.title: IELTS Writing Task 2: Cooking at Home
1.text: Nowadays, many people choose to buy fast food or eat in restaurants instead of cooking meals at home. Why do you think this is happening? Is this a positive or negative development for people's health and lifestyle? Give reasons for your answer and include relevant examples from your own experience. Write at least 150 words.

2.title: IELTS Writing Task 1: Letter to a Hotel Manager
2.text:
You recently travelled to another city for a holiday and stayed in a hotel, but you experienced several problems during your stay.

Write a letter to the manager of the hotel. In your letter:
- Give details of your stay and why you chose this hotel
- Describe the problems you had during your stay
- Explain what you want the manager to do about the situation

Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses. Begin your letter as follows: Dear Sir or Madam,

2.title: IELTS Writing Task: Housing Options
2.text: Some people prefer to live in a house, while others think that living in an apartment is better. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 150 words.

2.title: IELTS Writing Task 2: Sports in Schools
2.text: Some people think that physical education and sports should be compulsory for all school students. Others believe that sports should be optional so students can focus on academic subjects. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

2.title: IELTS Writing Task 2: Travel Options
2.text:
Write about the following topic:

Some people prefer to travel to foreign countries for their holidays, while others think it is better to spend their holiday time in their home country.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

3.title: IELTS Writing Task 2: Cultural Identity and Globalization
3.text: Some people believe that globalization leads to the loss of traditional customs and national identities. Others argue that it helps people from different backgrounds understand each other better. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion. Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

3.title: IELTS Essay Task: Renting vs. Buying Housing
3.text:
In many countries today, an increasing number of young people prefer to rent housing rather than buy their own homes.

What are the reasons for this trend?
Do the advantages of renting a home outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

4.title: IELTS Writing Task 2: Public vs Private Transport
4.text: Some people believe that the most effective way to reduce traffic congestion in major cities is to increase the cost of driving private vehicles, while others argue that governments should focus on improving public transportation systems instead. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion. Include relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.

4.title: IELTS Academic Writing Task 2: Economic Growth
4.text:
Some people believe that the primary goal of a government should be to maximize economic growth. Others argue that other aspects, such as environmental sustainability and social equality, are more important for a nation's well-being.

Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

4.title: IELTS Writing Task 2: Economic Growth and Poverty
4.text: Some economists argue that rapid economic growth is the most effective way to eliminate global poverty, while others believe that such growth leads to severe environmental degradation and social inequality. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion. Include relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.

4.title: IELTS Writing Task 2: Hosting Major International Sports Events
4.text: Some people argue that hosting major international sports events, such as the Olympic Games or the World Cup, brings significant economic and social benefits to the host country. Others believe that the huge financial expenditure involved would be better spent on public services and local community sports facilities. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

0.title: IELTS Speaking Part 1: Food (A1-A2 Level)
0.text: In Part 1 of the IELTS Speaking test, the examiner asks you short questions about familiar everyday topics. Today, we will talk about food. Please answer these beginner questions clearly: 1. What is your favourite type of food? 2. Who usually cooks the main meals in your home? 3. Do you prefer eating at home or in restaurants? Why? 4. What do you like to eat for breakfast every morning? 5. Tell me about a traditional dish from your home country. 6. Do you like drinking hot tea or fresh coffee? 7. Is there any food that you dislike eating?

0.title: IELTS Speaking Part 1: History
0.text:
In Part 1 of the IELTS Speaking test, you will answer simple questions about familiar topics. Today, we are going to talk about history. Please answer these questions:
1. Did you like learning about history when you were at school? Why or why not?
2. How often do you visit historical places or museums in your town?
3. Do you prefer reading history books or watching movies about the past?
4. Can you name a famous historical person from your country? Why are they important?
Answer each question using simple sentences and speak as clearly as possible.

0.title: IELTS Speaking Part 1: Travel and Holidays
0.text:
In this IELTS Speaking Part 1 task, you will answer simple questions about travel and holidays.

Please answer the following questions:
1. Do you like traveling? Why or why not?
2. What is your favorite place to visit in your home country?
3. How do you usually travel when you go on holiday?
4. Who do you usually spend your holidays with?
5. Do you prefer traveling by train, bus, or airplane? Why?
6. What new country would you like to visit in the future?

Try to speak in full sentences and give clear, simple answers for each question today.

1.title: IELTS Speaking Part 1: Media
1.text:
In Part 1 of the official IELTS Speaking test, the examiner will ask you general questions about familiar topics. Please answer these five questions about media:

1. How do you usually get your news every day, and why do you choose this method?
2. Do you prefer reading news online or watching it on television?
3. Did you listen to the radio when you were a child?
4. What kind of social media apps do you use most often to stay updated?
5. Do you think older people and younger people read the same news topics? Why or why not?

1.title: IELTS Speaking Part 1: Language Learning (B1)
1.text:
In Part 1 of the IELTS Speaking test, the examiner will ask you general questions about yourself and a range of familiar topics.

Topic: Language Learning

Questions:
1. What foreign languages have you studied or would you like to learn?
2. How long have you been learning English?
3. What do you find most difficult about learning a new language?
4. Do you think it is important to learn a second language? Why or why not?
5. How do you prefer to practice speaking English outside of class?
6. Did you enjoy learning languages when you were at school?

1.title: IELTS Speaking Part 1: Media
1.text: In Part 1 of the IELTS Speaking test, the examiner asks general questions about familiar topics. Answer the following questions about media and news using clear pre-intermediate English. How do you usually check the news every day? Do you prefer reading printed newspapers or reading news online? Did you watch the news with your family when you were younger? How often do you use social media to find out about world events? Do you think it is important to follow international news? What kind of news topics do you find most interesting to read about in your daily free time?

3.title: IELTS Speaking Part 2: Ideal Housing
3.text: Describe a house or apartment you would like to live in in the future. You should say: where it would be located, what kind of accommodation it would be, what special features or rooms it would have, and explain why you would prefer to live in this particular home instead of where you currently reside. You will have one minute to prepare your talk and up to two minutes to speak. Try to use relevant housing vocabulary and clear sentence structures.

3.title: IELTS Speaking Part 2: Personal Finances and Economics
3.text:
Describe a time when you made a smart financial decision.

You should say:
- what the decision was
- when and why you made this choice
- how you managed your money or budget at that time

and explain why you think this was a wise economic decision in the long run.

3.title: IELTS Speaking Part 2: Useful Technology Prompt
3.text:
Describe a piece of technology (such as a smartphone, laptop, or smart watch) that you find very useful in your daily life.

You should say:
- What this piece of technology is
- How long you have been using it
- What specific tasks you use it for

And explain why you consider this technology to be so essential to your routine, and how your daily life would be different if you no longer had it.

3.title: IELTS Speaking Part 2: Science Subject
3.text: Describe a science subject that you enjoyed studying at school or university. You should say: what the subject was, when and where you studied it, what interesting things you learned, and explain why you enjoyed studying this science subject so much.

3.title: IELTS Speaking Part 2: A Healthy Habit
3.text: Describe a healthy habit that you have recently adopted or would like to start in the near future. You should say: what this habit involves, when and how you first learned about it, why you think it is beneficial for your physical or mental health, and explain what challenges you might face when trying to maintain this habit regularly in your daily routine. You will have one minute to prepare your talk and then you should speak for one to two minutes. Try to use varied upper-intermediate vocabulary related to health, exercise routines, balanced diet, and your overall personal well-being.

4.title: IELTS Speaking Part 2: Science Cue Card
4.text:
Describe an area of science that interests you.

You should say:
- what branch of science it is
- how you first became interested in it
- what practical applications or benefits it offers to modern society
- and explain why this specific field of study fascinates you.

Candidate Instructions: You will have precisely one minute to prepare your response and notes. You should then speak continuously for one to two minutes. To score at the B2+/C1 level, demonstrate advanced lexical resource by using complex topic-specific vocabulary related to scientific methodology, empirical research, groundbreaking discoveries, innovation, and technological advancement in your spoken presentation today.

5.title: IELTS Speaking Part 2: Social Media Influence
5.text:
Candidate Task Card: Social Media Influence

Describe a memorable occasion when content encountered on a social media platform significantly influenced a major personal decision or reshaped a strongly held opinion.

You should say:
- what the specific context or dilemma was
- which platform you were using and what media format you engaged with
- how the content altered your perspective, choices, or behavioral patterns

and explain whether, upon critical reflection, you consider this online influence to have yielded a positive or negative outcome for you, articulating the underlying reasons for your evaluation.

You will have one minute to prepare.

5.title: IELTS Speaking Part 2: Environmental Initiative
5.text: Describe an impactful environmental project or initiative that you are familiar with. You should say: what the project is and what its main objectives are, how you first learned about this initiative, what specific actions or measures were implemented to protect the environment, and explain why you consider this project to have been particularly successful in addressing local or global environmental issues. In addition, you should elaborate on how this initiative might inspire similar future projects in other communities or regions facing similar ecological challenges.

5.title: IELTS Speaking Part 2: Educational Course
5.text:
Describe an educational course or subject you found particularly engaging during your secondary or university studies that you would like to explore in greater depth in the future.

You should say:
- what the specific course or subject was and precisely when you studied it
- who the teacher or instructor was and what distinctive teaching methods they effectively employed
- what particular concepts, theoretical topics, or practical applications captured your intellectual curiosity

and explain in full detail how gaining deeper expertise in this academic discipline could significantly contribute to your long-term career trajectory, professional advancement, or personal intellectual growth and learning journey.
